SUNLESS
by Jimmy Coco

Internal process report · Email production system

How a campaign is built and structured.

Every Sunless campaign is a folder, and every email in it is generated — never hand-made. This report walks the full shape of that system: the anatomy of a campaign folder, the pipeline that produces it, and how one structured source file becomes rendered emails, Studio previews and Resend templates that can never drift apart. The Sydney stockist campaign is used as the worked example throughout, with real screenshots from the Studio and the rendered emails.

Prepared 15 July 2026 · Compiled from the jimmycoco repository as source of truth
Screenshots: Sunless Studio (current build of the deployed app) and the campaign's rendered HTML with sample merge data · Charts validated for colour-vision safety on this document's surface
Companion report: How subject lines are generated — the copy-level flow, guardrails and gates

Part one

The shape of a campaign: one folder, five files, one contract

A campaign is not scattered across tools — it is a single folder under email/campaigns/, named <market>-<audience>-<action>. The folder is the complete campaign: strategy, copy, structured data, Studio metadata and generated output, side by side. This is the Sydney campaign exactly as it exists in the repository:

au-sydney-salon-stockist/
The campaign — everything below travels together
├─ README.md
The brief. Goal, audience, market, offer, cadence table, exit and stop conditions, exclusions, unresolved approval tokens, compliance notes
├─ sequence.md
The human-readable copy. Subject options A/B/C, preview text and the complete plain-text body for every email — what a reviewer reads
├─ email-data.json
The single content source. Brand defaults plus one structured record per email — the only input the renderer accepts
├─ studio.json
Studio metadata. Display name, market, status, owner, hook, and one timeline day per message — the Studio discovers the folder from this
├─ whatsapp.md
Companion channel (only when the campaign uses one). The interleaved WhatsApp track with its own compliance rules
└─ emails/*.html
Generated output. One branded HTML file per email, produced by the shared master template — never edited by hand

Two of these files carry the same copy on purpose. sequence.md is for people; email-data.json is for the renderer — and a standing consistency rule requires them to stay semantically equivalent, so what the reviewer approved is always what gets rendered. Here is the same Sydney opener in both forms:

## EMAIL 1 — Opener (Day 0) · send as plain text

Subject A: A sun-safe glow for {{salon_name}}?
Subject B: a Sydney glow, minus the Sydney sun
Subject C: {{first_name}} — before the summer rush
Preview:   The professional tan behind Jimmy Coco's work — a
           complimentary trial for your booth before summer.

sequence.md — subjects are always drafted as options, with preview text paired to the chosen line.

{
  "output":   "emails/1-opener.html",
  "title":    "A sun-safe glow for {{salon_name}}?",
  "preview":  "The professional tan behind Jimmy Coco's work — …",
  "eyebrow":  "A note for {{salon_name}}",
  "headline": "A Sydney glow, without the Sydney sun.",
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "paragraph", "html": "Hi {{first_name}}," },
    { "type": "offer",     "html": "Could I post {{salon_name}} a
      <strong>complimentary trial</strong> … no cost, no commitment?" },
    { "type": "cta",       "label": "Post me a trial", "url": "…" }
  ]
}

email-data.json — the same message as structured blocks. Unknown facts stay as {{tokens}}; nothing is invented.

The one rule that protects everything: generated HTML is never the editable source. To change an email you change email-data.json and sequence.md, then rebuild. To change how every email looks, you change the shared master template once — with approval — and rebuild all campaigns together.

Part two

The production pipeline: request to reviewable draft

Anyone can start a campaign with a plain-language request — no schemas, no file names, no template knowledge. From there the pipeline is fixed, and each stage produces a concrete artifact:

1Request → brief"Build a campaign for Sydney onboarding salon stockists" becomes market, audience, outcome, offer, cadence, exclusions and handoff.
2Compliance preflightThe governing playbooks and closest comparable campaign are read; lifecycle collisions checked. Proceeds only on READY TO PRODUCE.
3Facts resolved or tokenisedUnknown prices, terms and claims become explicit approval tokens — never plausible-sounding copy.
4Source files authoredREADME, sequence.md, email-data.json, studio.json — original strategy and copy for this audience, in the approved voice.
5Registered, disabledThe campaign joins the shared builder and the send registry with enabled: false. Building never authorises sending.
6HTML generatednode email/campaigns/_shared/build-all.js renders every email through the master template, enforcing asset governance.
7ValidatedManifest validation, the test suite and the Studio build must pass. Any failure is a release blocker.
8Studio discoveryThe Studio finds the folder automatically via studio.json — no UI code changes, ever.
9Production reportChanged paths, sources read, outstanding tokens, gate results — and one permitted status, none of which send email.

The statuses a campaign can hold

Draft — not approved for send Ready for human review Changes required Blocked

Ready to send is deliberately not on the list — it requires a named human approving the current copy, facts, assets, recipients and rendered output, and even then the send path stays double-locked: the registry entry must be enabled: true and the environment must have EMAIL_LIVE_MODE on.

Part three

The worked example: Sydney salon stockist recruitment

The request was one sentence — "build a campaign for Sydney, Australia for onboarding potential salon stockists." The pipeline turned it into a five-email cold outreach sequence with a WhatsApp companion track, a distinct sun-safety and humidity angle (so it never duplicates the national AU campaign), mutual-suppression rules, and a handoff into the existing post-sample account flow the moment a salon replies.

Multichannel cadence — three weeks, ten touches, two channels

Email carries the argument; WhatsApp accelerates between touches. Both tracks stop the instant a salon replies on either channel.

1WhatsApp 1Warm intro + trial offer

6WhatsApp 2Trial nudge
8Email 3Two revenue lines
9WhatsApp 3Two ways to earn + call ask

Part four

One source, many surfaces — and why they can't drift

The reason the folder contract matters is what happens downstream. A single email-data.json feeds four surfaces: the generated HTML in emails/, the Studio's live preview, the published Resend templates, and the send registry that operates the campaign. Because all four descend from one source, a read-only drift check (npm run templates:check) can verify — byte for byte — that what is published in Resend is exactly what the repository would generate.

One renderer, every campaign — rendered branded emails per campaign

All 30 generated by the same master template; a single approved change to it updates every campaign on the next build. Sydney highlighted.

The Studio's Live emails view is the human checkpoint on that chain — the rendered HTML, the subject and preview as the inbox will pair them, sample merge data, and the message's place in the sequence, all in one screen:

Live emails view, Sydney email 01. The preview is the actual generated file; the sample-data toggle fills {{tokens}} the way the ESP will. "Read directly from source — rebuild and refresh."

The operational layer, in one excerpt

{
  id: 'au-sydney-salon-stockist',
  name: 'Sydney Stockist Recruitment',
  enabled: false,            // lock 1 — stays false until approved
  timezone: 'Australia/Sydney',
  localSendHour: 10,
  exitEvents: ['reply', 'trial_requested', 'unsubscribe', …],
  steps: [
    { day: 0,  templateAlias: 'au-sydney-stockist-1-opener',  templateId: '49f9…' },
    { day: 3,  templateAlias: 'au-sydney-stockist-2-…',       templateId: '2127…' },
    …
  ],
}

shared/campaign-registry.js — timing, template IDs and exit events. The worker can only send when enabled is true and EMAIL_LIVE_MODE is on (lock 2).

"Read first. Use the master. Preserve truth. Generate from structured data. Stop when blocked. Require human approval."
